title: AI Model Training & Inference Operations Core v1

domain.name: AI Model Training & Inference Operations
domain.description: Practical dataset preparation, fine-tuning concepts, evaluation, inference, quantization, GPU and VRAM planning, checkpoints, reproducibility, local deployment, and model lifecycle operations.

competencies.name: Dataset Curation & Splitting
competencies.description: Create clean, representative training, validation, and test data with provenance.
competencies.purpose: Prevent data quality and leakage problems from invalidating model results.

units.title: Dataset workflow
units.content: Define target behavior; collect permitted examples with provenance; deduplicate; normalize formats; label consistently; separate train, validation, and test by leakage-aware rules; document exclusions and known bias.

units.title: Dataset failures
units.content: Avoid evaluating on training duplicates, mixing future information into training for time-based tasks, unclear licensing or provenance, and balancing data solely by raw count without task relevance.

units.title: Better data beats more noisy data
units.content: Additional examples help only when they add relevant signal; duplicated or contradictory examples can degrade training.

drills.title: Audit a fine-tuning dataset
drills.prompt: Review a dataset for duplicates, leakage, labeling consistency, and provenance.

competencies.name: Fine-Tuning, LoRA & Adaptation Strategy
competencies.description: Choose between prompting, retrieval, adapters, fine-tuning, and full training based on the problem.
competencies.purpose: Use the least expensive method that changes the required behavior.

units.title: Not every knowledge gap needs training
units.content: Fresh facts and private documents often belong in retrieval; style or format consistency may suit adapters; fundamental capability changes may require deeper training.

units.title: Adaptation decision workflow
units.content: Define failure mode; test prompt or system changes; test retrieval if issue is knowledge access; consider LoRA or adapters for behavior and style; define training only if evidence shows it is needed; set evaluation before training.

units.title: Adaptation failures
units.content: Avoid fine-tuning to memorize frequently changing facts, training before building an eval set, and assuming more epochs always improve behavior.

drills.title: Choose an adaptation method
drills.prompt: For several local assistant problems, decide prompting, RAG, LoRA, or full fine-tuning.

competencies.name: Training Runs, Hyperparameters & Checkpoints
competencies.description: Plan learning rate, effective batch, epochs or steps, warmup, precision, checkpoints, and early stopping.
competencies.purpose: Run controlled experiments instead of changing many variables blindly.

units.title: Training experiment workflow
units.content: Set baseline; choose one primary hypothesis; define learning rate and effective batch; choose max steps or epochs; log train and validation metrics; checkpoint regularly; stop on divergence or overfit; retain run configuration.

units.title: Change one major variable at a time
units.content: Training experiments become uninterpretable when dataset, optimizer, learning rate, and schedule all change together.

units.title: Training failures
units.content: Avoid judging only training loss, overwriting best checkpoints, untracked seed or config changes, and continuing after validation clearly degrades.

drills.title: Design a LoRA experiment
drills.prompt: Create an experiment plan with baseline, metrics, learning-rate search, checkpoints, and stopping rules.

competencies.name: Evaluation & Benchmark Design
competencies.description: Measure model quality against task-specific examples, baselines, and failure categories.
competencies.purpose: Know whether a model change actually improved the target behavior.

units.title: Evaluation workflow
units.content: Define success criteria; build a frozen representative eval set; include normal and edge cases; compare baseline and candidate blinded where possible; record per-category results; inspect regressions, not just average score.

units.title: Evaluation failures
units.content: Avoid evaluating only cherry-picked demos, changing the test set after seeing failures, using one aggregate score that hides severe regressions, and treating subjective preference as objective without a rubric.

units.title: Eval set is a product specification in examples
units.content: A good eval set encodes what behavior matters and should remain stable across experiments.

drills.title: Compare two local models
drills.prompt: Design an evaluation for coding and helpdesk tasks with quality, latency, and reliability metrics.

competencies.name: Quantization, Precision & Memory Planning
competencies.description: Choose model precision and quantization based on hardware, quality, context, and throughput needs.
competencies.purpose: Fit useful models into available GPU and CPU memory without blind trial and error.

units.title: Weights are only part of memory
units.content: KV cache, activations, runtime buffers, context length, batch size, and offload also affect memory consumption.

units.title: Memory planning workflow
units.content: Identify hardware VRAM and RAM; estimate weight footprint by precision; account for context and KV cache plus batch; choose quantization; test representative context; monitor peak memory and quality; record stable config.

units.title: Memory failures
units.content: Avoid sizing only from parameter count, pushing context until OOM with no headroom, and assuming the smallest quantization is always best for quality.

drills.title: Plan an 8GB VRAM deployment
drills.prompt: Choose a model, quantization, and context strategy for a local assistant on 8GB VRAM.

competencies.name: Inference Serving, Batching & Latency
competencies.description: Operate local model servers with context, concurrency, streaming, batching, and timeout controls.

units.title: Serving workflow
units.content: Choose runtime and model format; configure context and concurrency for hardware; enable streaming if useful; set timeouts and queue limits; measure cold and warm latency; monitor memory; isolate slow requests; define fallback behavior.

units.title: Serving failures
units.content: Avoid unlimited concurrency on a single GPU, giant context defaults, restarting on every slow request, and measuring only tokens per second without end-to-end latency.

units.title: Throughput and latency trade off
units.content: Batching can improve total throughput while making an individual interactive request wait longer; optimize for workload.

drills.title: Tune a local model server
drills.prompt: Plan concurrency, context, streaming, and queue limits for interactive desktop use.

competencies.name: GPU, CUDA & Runtime Debugging
competencies.description: Diagnose driver, CUDA, framework, DLL, kernel, precision, and out-of-memory failures.
competencies.purpose: Separate environment failures from model or workflow failures.

units.title: GPU debug workflow
units.content: Capture exact error and versions; confirm GPU visibility; inspect driver and runtime compatibility; verify framework build; reproduce a minimal tensor or model test; monitor VRAM; then add application layers back one at a time.

units.title: Prove the smallest GPU operation first
units.content: A minimal framework allocation or matmul can separate CUDA and runtime setup from application-specific code.

units.title: GPU debugging failures
units.content: Avoid reinstalling everything before recording versions, mixing incompatible CUDA wheels across environments, and treating every OOM as a driver problem.

drills.title: Diagnose a CUDA DLL or runtime error
drills.prompt: Create an isolation sequence for a Python environment that cannot initialize GPU acceleration.

competencies.name: Model Versioning, Reproducibility & Deployment
competencies.description: Track model files, adapters, tokenizer and config, prompts, eval results, and runtime settings across releases.
competencies.purpose: Know exactly what model configuration produced a result and roll back safely.

units.title: Model release workflow
units.content: Assign model and adapter version; record base model checksum or reference; preserve tokenizer and config; record prompt or template and runtime parameters; attach eval results; stage deployment; monitor; retain rollback artifact.

units.title: Lifecycle failures
units.content: Avoid renaming model files without provenance, overwriting adapters, changing prompt templates without versioning, and deploying a quantized conversion that was never evaluated.

units.title: The deployable unit is more than weights
units.content: Behavior depends on tokenizer, chat template, system prompt, adapter, quantization, context settings, and runtime.

drills.title: Define a local model release record
drills.prompt: Specify what must be captured for a reproducible FREEOS model deployment.
